docs.lit.component: `Lit` is the canvas's ONE light — a root-only field, because there is no per-piece lamp. What
it answers is the direction every shadow falls: `angle` says where the light stands, degrees
clockwise from +x, and the fall is its exact opposite. A desk that never declared a lamp is lit
by the stock one — top-right of the frame, shadows down-left — so shadow casters never stand
## The frame — whose corner the lamp hangs in
`viewer` (the default): the light stands in the corner of the SCREEN, so a shadow reads as
height the same way from every seat — at the price of the lamp orbiting the desk as the camera
turns. `world`: the lamp is nailed over the DESK, physical, and the fall turns with it. The two
differ only while a camera is turned; the frame is declared now and felt the day the camera
arrives — one formula in one place already reads it.
docs.lit.light: Two pieces of different height under one lamp. Walk `angle` and every fall turns together:
the light is the root's, and a piece cannot bring its own. The taller piece throws the longer
shadow — the lamp owns the direction, the height owns the length. `frame` picks whose corner
the lamp hangs in; without a camera to turn, `viewer` and `world` agree, and that agreement is
the point — the choice is data waiting for the camera, not a mode of this scene.
